_comment: Static image lookup for medical notes. findings = visual signs/scores by keyword. topic_images = disease → [finding keys to embed].

ecthyma gangrenosum.caption: Ecthyma gangrenosum — black necrotic lesion, pathognomonic of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in febrile neutropenia

disseminated gonococcal infection.caption: Disseminated gonococcal infection — pustular/hemorrhagic skin lesions

janeway lesions.caption: Janeway lesions — painless hemorrhagic macules on palms/soles (Infective Endocarditis)

osler nodes.caption: Osler nodes — painful subcutaneous nodules on fingertips (Infective Endocarditis)

splinter hemorrhages.caption: Splinter hemorrhages — linear subungual hemorrhages (Infective Endocarditis)

malar rash.caption: Malar rash (butterfly rash) — spares nasolabial folds, pathognomonic of SLE

gottron's papules.caption: Gottron's papules — violaceous papules over MCP/PIP joints (Dermatomyositis)

palpable purpura.caption: Palpable purpura — raised non-blanching lesions (leukocytoclastic vasculitis)

erythema marginatum.caption: Erythema marginatum — serpiginous migratory rash (Acute Rheumatic Fever, Jones criteria)

spider angiomas.caption: Spider angiomas — central arteriole with radiating vessels, sign of chronic liver disease

caput medusae.caption: Caput medusae — dilated periumbilical veins, sign of portal hypertension

terry's nails.caption: Terry's nails (leukonychia) — white nails with distal brown band, chronic liver disease

koilonychia.caption: Koilonychia (spoon nails) — concave nails, sign of iron deficiency anemia

roth spots.caption: Roth spots — white-centered retinal hemorrhages (Infective Endocarditis)

curb-65.caption: CURB-65 score — Pneumonia severity (Confusion, Urea>7, RR≥30, BP<90/60, Age≥65)

sofa score.caption: SOFA Score — Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (Sepsis-3)

meld score.caption: MELD Score — Model for End-Stage Liver Disease

mascc score.caption: MASCC Score — Risk index for febrile neutropenia (≥21 = low risk)

cha2ds2-vasc.caption: CHA₂DS₂-VASc Score — Stroke risk in atrial fibrillation

has-bled.caption: HAS-BLED Score — Bleeding risk in anticoagulated AF patients

killip classification.caption: Killip Classification — Heart failure severity in ACS

grace score.caption: GRACE Score — Risk stratification in ACS

spherocytes.caption: Spherocytes — small, round, dense RBCs without central pallor (Warm AIHA, Hereditary Spherocytosis)

schistocytes.caption: Schistocytes (helmet cells) — fragmented RBCs in MAHA (TTP, HUS, DIC)

bite cells.caption: Bite cells (degmacytes) — notched RBCs after splenic removal of Heinz bodies (G6PD deficiency)

heinz bodies.caption: Heinz body formation in G6PD deficiency — denatured hemoglobin precipitates after oxidative stress

target cells.caption: Target cells (codocytes) — bulls-eye appearance, seen in Thalassemia, Liver disease, post-splenectomy

pencil cells.caption: Pencil cells (elliptocytes) — elongated hypochromic RBCs in iron deficiency anemia

hypochromic microcytes.caption: Hypochromic microcytic anemia — pale, small RBCs with increased central pallor (IDA)

hypersegmented neutrophils.caption: Hypersegmented neutrophil (>5 lobes) — pathognomonic of megaloblastic anemia (B12/Folate deficiency)

teardrop cells.caption: Teardrop cells (dacrocytes) — pear-shaped RBCs in Thalassemia and myelofibrosis

rbc agglutination.caption: RBC agglutination (grape-like clumps) — Cold AIHA / cold agglutinin disease

rouleaux.caption: Rouleaux formation — RBC stacking like coins, seen in Multiple Myeloma (high paraprotein)

atrophic glossitis.caption: Atrophic glossitis (Hunters glossitis) — smooth, red tongue with loss of papillae (B12 deficiency)

angular cheilitis.caption: Angular cheilitis — fissuring at corners of mouth (Iron deficiency anemia, B2 deficiency)

chipmunk face thalassemia.caption: Chipmunk face / frontal bossing — thalassemia major facies due to erythroid hyperplasia expanding marrow

fibromuscular_dysplasia_(renal_artery_st.url: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Renal artery angiography in a patient with fibromuscular dysplasia (1).jpg
fibromuscular_dysplasia_(renal_artery_st.caption: Renal artery angiography in a 35-year-old woman with unexplained hypertension, showing the classic "string-of-beads" sign (indicated by arrows) characteristic of medial fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) of the renal artery.

abdominal_striae_in_cushing's_syndrome.caption: Wide, violaceous abdominal striae (purple stretch marks) in a patient with Cushing's syndrome, a classic physical sign indicative of glucocorticoid excess causing secondary hypertension.

adrenal_cortical_adenoma_in_conn's_syndr.caption: Gross pathology of a sliced adrenal gland showing a well-circumscribed, yellow aldosterone-producing cortical adenoma in a patient with Conn's syndrome (primary aldosteronism).

hypertensive_retinopathy.caption: Fundoscopic examination showing advanced hypertensive retinopathy with retinal hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots, hard exudates, and optic disc edema associated with severe, uncontrolled hypertension.

left_ventricular_hypertrophy_on_ecg.caption: Twelve-lead ECG showing left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) with characteristic secondary repolarization abnormalities (ST-T strain pattern), a common target organ complication of chronic hypertension.

manual_blood_pressure_measurement_tools.caption: An aneroid sphygmomanometer and manual stethoscope, which are standard clinical diagnostic instruments used for evaluating and monitoring hypertension.

renal_artery_stenosis_(fibromuscular_dys.caption: Renal artery angiography in a 35-year-old woman with unexplained hypertension showing the typical 'string-of-beads' sign (indicated by arrows) characteristic of fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) involving an accessory left renal artery.

cushing's_syndrome_purple_striae.caption: Wide, violaceous abdominal striae in a patient with Cushing's syndrome, a classic secondary cause of resistant and refractory hypertension due to chronic cortisol excess.
